report.tagline: Microsoft's chat, meetings and calling app for work, sold as part of Microsoft 365.
report.simpleSummary: Microsoft Teams is where many office workers chat, join video meetings and share files. It comes with Microsoft 365, the same subscription that gives you Word, Excel and Outlook, so many companies get it without buying anything extra. You can message coworkers, hold meetings with hundreds of people, and edit Office files together. Microsoft makes money because companies pay for Microsoft 365 per person each month.

overview.whatItDoes: Teams combines group chat, video meetings, phone calling and file sharing in one app. It is built into Microsoft 365, so files live in SharePoint and OneDrive, calendars in Outlook, and documents open in Word or Excel inside the chat. Copilot AI can summarise meetings and chats.
howItWorks: A company buys Microsoft 365 and IT turns on Teams for every employee.
Employees chat one-on-one or in teams and channels, and join meetings from Outlook invites.
Files shared in Teams are stored in SharePoint or OneDrive and can be edited together.
Teams Phone lets people make and receive normal phone calls, for an extra fee.
Teams Premium and Copilot add AI meeting notes, recaps and translations for extra per-user fees.
Teams Rooms hardware turns meeting rooms into video rooms.
overview.valueProposition: One app for chat, meetings, calls and Office files, already paid for in your Microsoft 365 plan, with the security IT teams trust.

businessModel.summary: Teams makes money mainly by making Microsoft 365 worth paying for. Companies pay per user per month for Microsoft 365, and Teams is part of that or a cheap add-on. Microsoft earns more from add-ons like Teams Premium, Teams Phone, Rooms and Copilot.

revenueStreams.detail: Per user per month, with Teams included in many plans and sold separately in new enterprise plans since 2024 and in the EU.

revenueStreams.stream: Teams Essentials and Teams Enterprise standalone
revenueStreams.detail: About $4 to $5.25 per user per month.
Add-on for advanced meetings and AI, about $10 per user per month.
Phone calling add-on, plus calling plans.
About $30 per user per month for AI across Microsoft 365, including Teams.

businessModel.pricing: Free personal version. Teams Essentials about $4 per user per month. Microsoft 365 Business Basic and Standard include Teams, from about $6 and $12.50 per user per month in the US. In India, Business Basic is around ₹145 per user per month. Enterprise plans priced with or without Teams.
costDrivers: Cloud capacity for video meetings, run on Azure
AI model costs for Copilot features
Engineering for desktop, mobile and web apps
businessModel.unitEconomics: A company on Microsoft 365 Business Standard pays about $12.50 per user per month, or $150 a year. Teams is one part of that. Video meetings cost more to run than chat, maybe a few dollars per heavy user per year, but Microsoft already runs Azure at huge scale, so the cost is low. The real money is in upsells: one user with Copilot adds $360 a year. Because Teams makes customers stay on Microsoft 365, its value is more in keeping customers than in its own fee. Rough estimates.

howTheyGetUsers: Bundling: included with Microsoft 365, which most large companies already buy
Replacing Skype for Business, which Microsoft retired
COVID remote work pushed meetings online
Microsoft's huge sales and partner network
whatBringsUsersBack: Meetings scheduled in Outlook open in Teams
Files and channels for each project
Default auto-start on Windows work laptops
growth.moat: Most big companies already pay for Microsoft 365, so Teams is the default. It is tied to Outlook, Office files, security and identity in a way rivals cannot copy. The EU forced a split in Europe in 2025, but most customers still buy the full bundle.

competitors.name: Slack (Salesforce)
competitors.positioning: Chat-first work app loved by tech teams.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Teams is bundled and stronger on meetings and Office files. Slack has a better chat experience and more integrations.

competitors.name: Zoom
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Teams wins in big companies on bundle and Office ties. Zoom is easier for outside guests.

competitors.name: Google Workspace (Meet and Chat)
competitors.positioning: Google's bundle of email, docs, chat and video.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Teams fits Windows and Office-first companies. Google fits browser-first and startups.

competitors.name: Webex (Cisco)
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Teams has the Office bundle; Webex has strong meeting hardware.

improvementIdeas.idea: A 'lite' mode that loads only chat and calendar for low-memory laptops
improvementIdeas.problem: Users complain Teams is slow and heavy.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: App load time and weekly active users

improvementIdeas.idea: Merge chats and channels into one simple inbox with filters
improvementIdeas.problem: People are confused about where to post.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More messages in shared spaces, less missed info.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Messages per user and missed-mention complaints

improvementIdeas.problem: Working with other companies is clunky.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More cross-company use, fewer people choosing Slack Connect or Zoom.

improvementIdeas.idea: Free Copilot meeting recap for 3 meetings a month on all plans
improvementIdeas.problem: Companies are unsure Copilot is worth $30.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More Copilot trials that convert to paid seats.

pmLessons: Distribution can beat a better product. Teams overtook Slack by coming with Office, not by having a nicer chat app.
Bundling invites regulators. Slack's 2020 complaint led to EU commitments in 2025.
A product people use because IT chose it can grow huge but still be disliked, which leaves room for rivals.
Upsells like Copilot work best when the base product is already a daily habit.

interviewQuestions.question: Why did Teams beat Slack in large companies?
interviewQuestions.hint: Distribution through Microsoft 365, the IT buyer, security, meetings during COVID. Contrast bottom-up vs top-down sales.

interviewQuestions.question: Users say Teams is slow. How would you prioritise fixing it?
interviewQuestions.hint: Measure load time and memory by device, find top slow flows, set a target, guardrail on features.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you measure Copilot's success inside Teams?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weekly use, meeting recaps viewed, time saved survey, Copilot seat renewal.

interviewQuestions.question: The EU forces Teams out of the bundle. What do you do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Price the standalone right, make it worth buying alone, improve interoperability, measure attach rate.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Teams' north star metric?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weekly engaged users, not licences sold. Break into activation, meetings, chat and add-ons.
